title: Tactile Agent — One demonstration, task-specific touch
purpose: Bottle-led framework film: show actual demonstration segments as flowchart nodes, control-authority badges, hand/object perception, relative retargeting, and a tactile primitive tree compiled into a task policy.

principles: White background, wide margins, large dark typography.
One relation per shot; line and node reveals follow the narration.
Use actual user footage; reproduce the clarity and pacing, not the reference branding or media.
Keep source videos large, captions below or beside the footage.

semantic_nodes.title: Approach cap
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Agent chooses a cap standoff; motion planning adapts the approach to the current robot and scene.

semantic_nodes.title: Grasp + press
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Preserve the grasp relation to the cap; press along the bottle axis; tactile response gates rotation.

semantic_nodes.title: Twist
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Rotate in the cap task frame; choose robot-feasible wrist travel and maintain contact.

semantic_nodes.title: Reset + regrasp
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Plan the wrist reset, restore the cap-contact relation, and re-establish the press gate.

semantic_nodes.title: Final turn + release
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Continue task-axis rotation until a tactile release candidate passes fresh stationary verification.

semantic_nodes.title: Lift cap
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Plan the lift after release; initial displacement is constrained along the live bottle axis.

semantic_nodes.title: Place aside
semantic_nodes.control_rule: Select a supported placement goal and plan the motion.
semantic_nodes.evidence: human demonstration only; Run16 robot evidence ends at cap lift

policy_code.caption: Illustrative task policy; helpers stop on failed contact or missing evidence.

helper_semantics.require: A failed contact or pressing predicate stops progression; the helper does not continue into motion.
helper_semantics.fresh_prepress_window: Establish a new stationary baseline before pressing, including after each regrasp.
helper_semantics.press_until_response: Use bounded axial pressing and fresh tactile evidence; stop if engagement cannot be established.
helper_semantics.release_candidate: After sufficient turning and a measured resistance peak: require two fresh low-resistance windows while contact remains present.
helper_semantics.stationary_confirm: Read a fresh stationary window and confirm retained contact and low resistance.
helper_semantics.twist_segment: One bounded geometric wrist segment in the cap task frame; first revolution downfeed, later turns helical upfeed.
helper_semantics.bounded_regrasp_cycles: The actual runner bounds twist steps, press attempts and wrist resets; the film condenses these budgets for readability.

run16.signal_units: Session-relative raw sensor units; not newtons or calibrated torque

scenes.title: From one demonstration to touch-guided action
scenes.narration: One demonstration. A robot plans the motion, transfers the interaction, and checks progress through touch.
scenes.visual: Open on the actual cap lift, then freeze and reveal three small labels.

scenes.title: Watch the human demonstration
scenes.narration: Here, a person presses and twists a safety cap, resets their grip, then removes it. The demonstration gives us the structure of a task.
scenes.visual: Play the actual effective interval, with a thin time ribbon marking the existing stage boundaries.

scenes.title: The agent organizes the task
scenes.narration: Each segment becomes a node: approach, grasp and press, twist, reset and regrasp, check release, lift, and place aside. The agent plans free motion. At contact, it preserves object-relative geometry. Touch governs transitions. Placement belongs to the human demonstration; the robot run ends at lift.
scenes.visual: Expand the time ribbon into seven video cards. Animate the twist–regrasp loop. Reveal PLAN, RELATIVE, and TOUCH badges at the relevant cards.
scenes.evidence_label: Seven semantic groups of eleven annotated source intervals

scenes.title: See the hand–object interaction
scenes.narration: Perception locates the object and follows the hand. Masks separate image regions; keypoints describe hand configuration. These overlays connect the task stages to visible evidence in the demonstration.
scenes.visual: Three synchronized moving crops from the same recorded demonstration: RGB, SAM 2.1 hand/object segmentation, and RTMPose-m Hand5 landmarks. Replay at 0.5x and display the source frame number.
scenes.on_screen: Recorded RGB / Hand + object masks / Hand keypoints
scenes.evidence_label: Derived visualization of the recorded demonstration

scenes.title: Preserve the relative interaction
scenes.narration: At contact, the hand's position and orientation are expressed relative to the object. A gripper adapter maps this relation to robot geometry. Grounding it in the current scene produces a robot target.
scenes.visual: Transform the contact panel into a clean object-frame equation. Animate the object and a gripper contact frame moving together; distinguish concept from observed 3-D quantities.
scenes.on_screen: HAND–CAP RELATION → GRIPPER–CAP RELATION → LIVE ROBOT TARGET
scenes.evidence_label: Retargeting concept; cap yaw is not observed

scenes.title: Plan what can change
scenes.narration: For free-space stages, the agent sets a goal. A motion planner connects that goal to the robot's current configuration.
scenes.visual: Pull the cyan approach/reset cards onto an agent→planner lane; keep the gold contact/axis lane fixed to the object.
scenes.evidence_label: Architecture; current robot runner is task-specific

scenes.title: Choose touch for this task
scenes.narration: The tactile library branches into images, forces, and torques. Each supports different contact primitives. For this bottle, select contact, pressing, contact retention, and release. The recorded controller uses changes in raw force channels. Torque is a possible input, but was not used in this run.
scenes.visual: Reveal a three-branch tactile tree: contact images, force response, torque response. Highlight contact/press response and retention/release proxy leaves for the bottle task; retain unselected image and torque branches.
scenes.on_screen: TACTILE LIBRARY → TASK SELECTION → STAGE PREDICATES
scenes.evidence_label: Run16: raw Fz proxies; no calibrated torque claim

scenes.title: Turn the selection into a policy
scenes.narration: The selected primitives become task conditions. This illustrative policy shows the composition: wait for pressing evidence, rotate while contact remains, reset and regrasp when needed, then verify release before lifting. The recorded hardware executor is task-specific.
scenes.visual: Reveal the final fourteen-line illustrative task policy, with contact, press, retention and release conditions listed alongside it. Highlight the code as its conditions are explained.
scenes.evidence_label: Illustrative pseudocode; actual execution uses a deterministic task runner

scenes.title: Execute the loop
scenes.narration: Now the robot executes. Pressing evidence permits the first twist. The first turn feeds down; later turns follow the thread upward. Between segments, the robot unloads, resets its wrist, and regrasps. Six ninety-degree segments produce five hundred and forty degrees, with five automatic reset cycles.
scenes.visual: Show recorded Run16 robot video at 8.7x; illuminate real twist intervals and group the intervening unload/reset/regrasp phases. Six segment markers show task-axis rotation.

scenes.title: Let the evidence authorize the lift
scenes.narration: Turn count alone does not permit lifting. Resistance must build, then stay low in fresh measurements while contact remains. A stationary check confirms release. The final reading falls below the recorded threshold, and the controller permits a thirty-millimetre lift.
scenes.visual: Show four discrete logged windows with the final release limit and retained-contact condition; after verification, play the actual 30 mm cap lift at 1x.
scenes.on_screen: PEAK → SUSTAINED DROP + CONTACT → VERIFIED → LIFT
scenes.evidence_label: Discrete logged raw-sensor windows; trace reconstructed from the execution log

scenes.title: One framework, explicit responsibilities
scenes.narration: Tactile Agent connects demonstrated intent and object-relative interaction with robot motion, supervised by task-specific touch.
scenes.visual: Return to the seven-node graph, the tactile tree and the robot result; finish with a simple title card.
scenes.on_screen: Tactile Agent — Learn the intent. Feel the interaction.
scenes.evidence_label: Recorded evidence ends at cap lift

evidence_boundaries: Human demonstration begins with the bottle already upright.
No second human hand stabilizes the bottle in the demonstrated interval.
The round cap has no observable unique visual yaw.
Human video does not provide tactile force labels.
Seven semantic groups summarize eleven annotated demo intervals, including three demonstrated regrasp intervals.
Robot Run16 performs five wrist-reset/regrasp cycles; it does not copy the human repeat count.
Run16 decision signals are raw Fz proxies, not calibrated forces or torques.
No synchronized tactile RGB exists for Run16; do not present other-session tactile images as synchronized footage.
Run16 ends at cap lift. Place aside is present only in the human demonstration.
Generic task compilation and the illustrative code diagram explain the architecture; current hardware execution is task-specific.
